answers.explanation: Physical carries bits, data link carries frames, network carries packets. IP calls its packets datagrams.
Forwarding is the local, per-packet step: input link to output link, using the forwarding table.
Planning the whole route is routing. Picking the right exit at one interchange is forwarding.
The forwarding table (often loosely called the routing table) maps destinations to output links.
The IP addresses stay the same end to end. It's the frame, and its MAC addresses, that is replaced at every hop.
Forwarding is per packet, in nanoseconds. Routing runs every few seconds or minutes, in software, and only updates the table.
That's the router's job at every hop: de-encapsulate to layer 3, decide, re-encapsulate for the next link.
Switches work at layer 2, within a LAN. Routers work at layer 3, between networks.
